name: filebrowser-833d9088-blind29

# File Browser answers wrongly all over: diagnose 29 injected one-line faults without a test suite

This is a server that lets people sign in, browse a tree of documents on disk, add new ones, and hand links to outsiders. Almost nothing about it behaves the way it used to. The repository has received 29 separate undocumented edits. They are spread widely enough that repairing the first thing you notice leaves most of the trouble in place.

Signing in when identities come from an external helper program is wrong in several ways. The very first sign-in by somebody who has no account yet ends in an error instead of quietly creating one, since the lookup that is supposed to tolerate "no such account" now treats that answer as fatal. When the helper does name a home folder for the person it vouches for, that name is thrown away and one derived from the login name is saved in its place, and the result is reported as though no home folder had been named explicitly. And the verdict word the helper prints, the one that tells the server to accept or to block the attempt, is no longer read, so a helper that blocks and a helper that accepts look identical to whatever asked — even though the login name and password still reach the helper through its environment and are never pasted into the program line it is started with.
